summary.summary: Cover report for Sandwell's draft 2025/26 Statement of Accounts, published on the council website on 30 June 2026 in line with the statutory deadline; Grant Thornton began fieldwork on 13 July 2026, targeting audit completion by 10 November and final publication by 30 November 2026, well inside the 31 January 2027 backstop. The draft CIES reports net income of £109.6m, with General Fund balances up £10.6m, HRA balances down £1.1m and capital-programme reserves up £15.8m — a strengthening usable-reserves position. One open item: a specialist adviser is reviewing all four PFI financial models for consistency and compliance, and the council cannot yet quantify what adjustments that review will feed into the final accounts. Group accounts consolidate the wholly-owned Sandwell Children's Trust.

signals.headline: Draft 2025/26 accounts published 30 June 2026 on the statutory deadline; General Fund balances improved £10.6m, but a review of four PFI financial models is ongoing with the impact not yet quantifiable
signals.why: The reserves direction is positive for creditors, but the PFI model review is an open-ended adjustment risk sitting in the draft until the November 2026 audit completion.

news_drafts.headline: Sandwell schools grant deficit £6.296m at March 2026; government confirms funding at 90%
news_drafts.lead:
Sandwell's cumulative deficit on the dedicated schools grant (DSG), the government grant that funds schools, was £6.296m at 31 March 2026, against a £2.6m surplus at the end of 2024/25. The council's external auditor reports this in its interim annual report, which gives a forecast of £34.4m for 2026/27. The council has received approval and confirmation of funding at 90% of the 31 March 2026 deficit under the High Needs Stability Grant, subject to its special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) Reform Plan.

The DSG overspent by £11.6m in 2025/26, with £8.7m of it in high needs, the part of school funding for children with SEND. The auditor's report forecasts the deficit at £51.5m in 2027/28 and £126.3m in 2030/31, both after mitigations. It says the council submitted its reform plan to the Department for Education on time, and that future grant amounts and timing are not yet known.

The council's strategic risk register, as at October 2026, lists SEND placements as Red and travel as Green. A separate register entry moves the placements risk score from 16 (Red) to 9 (Amber), against a March 2027 target, and cites a 2025/26 internal audit of SEND placement costs that gave limited assurance. The register says the council will need a DSG mitigation plan, scheduled for winter 2026/27, so that there is "no (or limited) impact on the General Fund".
news_drafts.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council Interim Auditor's Annual Report for the Year Ending 31 March 2026

news_drafts.headline: Sandwell forecasts £34.7m high needs overspend in 2026/27, taking cumulative deficit to £40.753m
news_drafts.lead:
Sandwell Council forecasts a £34.7m overspend in 2026/27 on high needs, the part of the dedicated schools grant (the government grant that funds schools) that pays for children with special educational needs and disabilities. The cumulative high needs deficit would rise from £6.053m to £40.753m by the end of the year. The draft medium-term financial strategy says overspending is forecast to increase further in 2027/28.

The schools grant reserve has been in deficit since 1 April 2026, following the 2025/26 high needs overspend. A statutory override, a temporary government rule that keeps such a deficit off the main balance sheet, applies until March 2028. The strategy assumes £5.448m (90%) of government funding, subject to Department for Education approval. The council says government is likely to fund 90% of the deficits but has not confirmed it for 2026/27 or 2027/28. It expects about 10% of the cumulative deficit at March 2028 to become a charge on the General Fund, its main budget, from April 2028. Its Reserves Strategy in February 2027 will aim to address this by reallocating reserves.

SEND home to school transport carries a forecast pressure of £7.7m in 2027/28, which the paper attributes to a rising number of children with education, health and care plans. It proposes £7.7m of ongoing budget growth. A £604k Children and Education saving, rated red at quarter 1, will be removed from the 2027/28 budget through that increased allocation. Remaining red-rated efficiencies must be delivered from 1 April 2027.

news_drafts.headline: Sandwell forecasts £34.7m schools grant overspend for 2026/27, all of it in high needs
news_drafts.lead:
Sandwell Council forecasts a £34.7m overspend for 2026/27 on its dedicated schools grant, the government grant that funds schools. All of it is in high needs, the part of school funding for children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). The draft medium-term financial strategy puts the cumulative high needs deficit at £40.753m at year-end, up from £6.053m, and says demand for SEND services has risen beyond budgeted levels.

The government has announced it intends to fund 90% of high needs deficits built up to the end of 2025/26. The council assumes £5.448m, subject to Department for Education approval of a local SEND Reform Plan. If it is received, the year-end deficit would be £35.305m. The papers say the council will be reliant on government providing additional high needs funding in the current and future years. They say the 90% is not confirmed for 2026/27 and 2027/28.

A statutory override, a temporary government rule that keeps the deficit off the main balance sheet, runs to March 2028. The papers estimate around 10% of the cumulative deficit at that date is likely to become a charge to the General Fund, the council's main account for day-to-day spending. The cabinet report also gives a forecast budget pressure of £7.7m in 2027/28 on SEND home to school transport, because of rising numbers of children with education, health and care plans. It proposes £7.7m of ongoing growth for it.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council Interim Auditor's Annual Report for the Year Ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: Tipton new-build scheme responding to delays after contractor failure; Alfred Gunn House defects and cladding under active review
findings.detail: The paper says arrangements are being managed to support continued delivery at Tipton. At Alfred Gunn House, independent technical assessments and specialist commercial and legal advisers are being used on defects and contractual matters, which remain under active review.
findings.matters: A contractor failure on a new-build scheme and open cladding and contract disputes on another project are the kind of delivery and contingent-liability risks that affect capital budgets.
findings.quote: responding to delays on the Tipton new-build scheme following contractor failure

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council Interim Auditor's Annual Report for the Year Ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: Procurement waivers fell from 59 to 37 between April to September 2025 and the same period in 2026, a 37% reduction
findings.detail: The paper notes that most waivers still relate to direct awards and that waiver values were not reported, so the value of expenditure subject to waiver could not be assessed. No improvement recommendation was raised.
findings.matters: A falling waiver count is a measurable procurement control result, though the paper says the value of spend subject to waiver is unknown.
findings.quote: the number of waivers reducing from 59 to 37 between April-September 2025 and the same period in 2026

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council Interim Auditor's Annual Report for the Year Ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: General Fund reserve rises by £0.853m to £23.321m in the 2026/27 budget, maintained at around 5% of net revenue budget
findings.detail: The paper reports a balanced 2026/27 budget without drawing on the General Fund Reserve. The contribution to reserves is the first positive movement the paper records for the General Fund balance.
findings.matters: A reserve rebuilt to around 5% of net revenue budget is a measurable buffer that the paper says will need to absorb DSG and HRA pressures.
findings.figures: £0.853m contribution; £23.321m balance; c5% of net revenue budget
findings.quote: includes a contribution to the General Fund reserves of £0.853m

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council Interim Auditor's Annual Report for the Year Ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: HRA reserve balance was £50.052m at year end, with a £8.857m draw forecast for 2026/27 that would reduce it to £35.833m
findings.detail: The HRA outturn was an overspend of £1.098m, offset in full from HRA reserves. The paper says future draws in the MTFS would take the reserve below its 10% prudent balance. Improvement recommendation 3 covers business plan modelling.
findings.matters: Drawing the HRA reserve below its 10% prudent balance would weaken the financial resilience of the 27,700-home business plan.
findings.figures: £50.052m HRA reserve (year end); £1.098m 2025/26 overspend; £8.857m 2026/27 draw; £35.833m forecast balance; £137.8m 2025/26 rental income
findings.quote: the draw from reserves is forecast at £8.857m in 2026/27

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Sandwell Metropolitan Borough Council Interim Auditor's Annual Report for the Year Ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: General Fund Capital Programme spent £63.304m of £89.308m revised budget in 2025/26, with £25.810m slipped into 2026/27 and later years
findings.detail: The paper attributes the slippage mainly to schemes spanning financial years rather than budget underspends. The Disabled Facilities Grant programme had £6.678m of its £11.639m budget slipped. The HRA Capital Programme spent £62.330m of £92.552m, with a £30.222m variance slipped.
findings.matters: A 71% delivery rate on the General Fund programme with multi-year slippage shows the capacity and procurement risks other councils face when capital schedules are reprofiled.
findings.figures: £89.308m GF revised budget; £63.304m spent (71%); £25.810m slipped; £6.678m of £11.639m DFG budget slipped; £92.552m HRA budget; £62.330m spent (67%); £30.222m HRA variance
findings.quote: actual expenditure for the year totals £63.304m, representing 71% of the revised programme

daily_post.headline: Employer pension contribution rates for the West Midlands Pension Fund fall to 17.4% for 2026/27 from 24.6% in the previous three-year period, with rates projected to rise to 19.1% in the final two years of the MTFP.
daily_post.lead: Pension contribution rates are a recurring cost tied to the staffing base, and a rise after a fall is a movement a finance director would want to plan around.
